messages.content: The holds now give us two nights in Portland, September 13-15, and four nights in Bar Harbor, September 15-19. We need to settle the flights for two people before those holds expire.

I found two sensible structures. Round trip Denver-Portland is $1,036 total for two. The open-jaw version, Denver-Portland outbound and Bangor-Denver home, is $1,284 total. The open jaw costs $248 more but avoids returning the rental car in Portland on Friday.
What are the actual flight times, and how much driving does that save?

For Saturday, the lower round-trip fare offers a 9:05 a.m. Denver departure arriving Portland at 3:02 p.m., or a 1:20 p.m. departure arriving at 7:18 p.m.; both have one connection. The afternoon option adds $36 total for two. On Friday, returning through Portland means roughly 3 hours 15 minutes from Bar Harbor, plus a fuel stop and rental return. Bangor is about 1 hour 15 minutes away, so it saves around two hours of driving.
Use the 1:20 afternoon departure in the comparison. I would rather leave after lunch even though it means we lose that first Portland afternoon.

With that outbound, round trip through Portland becomes $1,072 for two. You would reach the hotel around 8:00-8:30 p.m., leaving Sunday as the only substantial Portland day. The open-jaw itinerary using the same outbound is $1,284, so its premium is $212.
And the Friday choices? I do not want a predawn drive out of Bar Harbor.

The Portland nonstop leaves at 5:35 p.m. and arrives Denver at 8:12 p.m. You would want to leave Bar Harbor around 12:45 p.m. The workable Bangor option leaves at 12:40 p.m., connects in New York, and reaches Denver at 6:48 p.m.; leaving Bar Harbor around 9:45 a.m. should provide a reasonable rental-car margin. There is also a cheaper 9:20 a.m. Bangor departure, but it would require leaving near 6:30 a.m.
Discard the 9:20. Compare the 12:40 Bangor flight with the 5:35 Portland flight in practical terms.

Portland costs $1,072 total airfare and entails about 3 hours 15 minutes of driving Friday. Bangor costs $1,284 and entails about 1 hour 15 minutes. Thus Bangor costs $212 more, or $106 per person, to save about two driving hours, while getting you home roughly 1 hour 24 minutes earlier. Its drawback is the connection: schedule disruption could delay the final leg, whereas Portland is nonstop.
Does the rental car change that arithmetic?

Possibly. The displayed base rental is $438 for Portland pickup and return. Portland pickup with Bangor return is $501, including a shown $63 one-way charge. If those totals hold, the open-jaw choice is $275 more overall: $212 additional airfare plus $63 additional car cost.
So we spend $275 to avoid two hours behind the wheel, get home earlier, and accept a connection. Is there any other loss at the Bar Harbor end?

Yes. The Bangor routing has you leave Bar Harbor about three hours earlier than the Portland routing, despite the shorter drive. You gain an easier drive and earlier arrival home, but give up most of Friday morning in Bar Harbor. The Portland flight preserves the morning and lunch there, then replaces that time with the longer drive.
That is the useful distinction. Rank them for this exact hotel sequence.

First: open jaw, Denver to Portland on September 13 and Bangor to Denver on September 19. It fits the two-night Portland/four-night Bar Harbor order cleanly and makes the final drive much easier; the practical premium is currently $275 for two. Second: round trip through Portland. It is the value choice and preserves more of Friday in Bar Harbor, but ends the trip with a long drive before the flight.
Choose the open jaw, but leave it unbooked. Give me the exact items to verify before the hotel holds expire.

Use the September 13 Denver-Portland itinerary departing at 1:20 p.m. and the September 19 Bangor-Denver itinerary departing at 12:40 p.m., for two adults, with a quoted airfare total of $1,284. Before purchase, verify the live fare, connection time, baggage terms, and seat availability; confirm that the Portland pickup/Bangor return rental still totals $501 with the one-way fee included; and confirm the two-night Portland and four-night Bar Harbor holds remain valid through purchase. Also recheck the Bangor return time because its narrower schedule is central to the choice. Nothing has been booked or changed.
